standard_prerequisites.name: The two formulas Phi_k and Psi_k and the Shore-blocking functional
standard_prerequisites.statement: Phi_k(G,x) states that there are indices below k, increasing in number x, at which the functional converges on the generic; Psi_k(G,x) states that the Shore-blocking functional Gamma_k converges at x, where Gamma_k is the functional of the Shore-blocking lemma for the ordinal alpha; the author's own definitions are retained at source lines 1250-1251 and the underlying lemma at 426-431.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the two formulas out of which the counted lemma lets the pair be chosen, and the quantities f_0 and f_1 in the proof are built from their values.

standard_prerequisites.name: Maximal trees of split pairs and their finite-tree forcing consequence
standard_prerequisites.statement: For every pair of Sigma^0_1 formulas and every condition there is a maximal tree of split pairs satisfying the pair, and if that tree is M-finite then some extension forces the two formulas at two indices and forces the negation of one of the next instances; retained with this card at source lines 1194-1196 and 1206-1215.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof obtains the maximal tree from the first statement and concludes with the second once it proves that the tree is M-finite, which is the only remaining step.

standard_prerequisites.name: Ordinal-valued rank of a finite tree and well-foundedness of the supremum
standard_prerequisites.statement: To each finite tree one assigns the ordinal obtained by summing, over the nodes, the ordinal omega raised to the sum of the two values f_0 and f_1 at the node, multiplied by the number of missing immediate successors; the hypothesis WF of the supremum of omega to the natural product with omega below alpha forbids an M-infinite decreasing sequence of such ordinals; the article uses these ordinals in the proof.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof defines exactly such a rank zeta_s for each approximating tree and shows that the ranks strictly decrease, which contradicts the well-foundedness hypothesis.

core_obligations: Apply the maximal-tree lemma to the chosen pair of formulas to obtain a maximal tree of split pairs satisfying it, and note that it remains to prove that this tree is M-finite in order to invoke the finite-tree forcing lemma (source line 1262).

Normalise the Shore-blocking functional by twisting so that convergence at an index forces convergence at every smaller index and the values form a strictly decreasing sequence of ordinals below the natural product of beta with k (source lines 1264-1268).

Argue by contradiction: assume the tree is M-infinite, let an increasing sequence of computable trees approach it and assume, without loss of generality, that consecutive trees differ (source line 1270).

Define the ordinal rank of a finite tree recursively: at each node take omega raised to the natural sum of the two values f_0 and f_1 at that node, multiplied by two minus the number of immediate successors, and add the ranks of the immediate successors (source lines 1272-1277).

Compare two consecutive trees: since they differ by a single node, the rank identity relating the two ranks at that node reduces to the inequality omega raised to the sum of the node values being strictly larger than twice omega raised to the sum at the new node, which holds for every choice of the two formulas because of how f_0 and f_1 behave on the two successors (source lines 1281-1287).

Conclude that the ranks form an M-infinite strictly decreasing sequence of ordinals below omega to the natural product of beta with omega, contradicting the well-foundedness hypothesis, so the tree is M-finite and the finite-tree forcing lemma gives the statement of the counted lemma (source lines 1289-1291).

proof_roadmap.step: Take the maximal tree and reduce the task to proving that it is M-finite.
Normalise Gamma_k and assume for contradiction an increasing approximation by distinct finite trees.
Define the ordinal rank of a finite tree and state the claim that the sequence of ranks strictly decreases.
Verify the claim by the local rank identity at the single node that changed.
Contradict well-foundedness, conclude M-finiteness and apply the finite-tree forcing lemma.

difficulty_reason: 计数单元是 arXiv:2402.11616v3 的 Lemma lem:sads-wf-forcing-wf-jump（源 1250-1259 行，证明 1261-1292 行）：对两种公式的任意组合与任意条件，存在扩展在两侧强制指定实例并使某一侧的下一实例被否定。证明的关键不是例行核验：作者先把问题化归为「证明那张极大树是 M-有限的」（1262 行），再假设树 M-无穷、取递增的有限树逼近（1270 行），然后为每棵树定义序数秩 ζ_s——在每个结点取 ω 的（f_0 ⨭ f_1）次幂乘（2 − 后继数）再对后继求和（1272-1277 行）；核心是验证 ζ_s 严格下降：两棵相邻树只差一个结点，秩恒等式归结为 ω^{f_0+f_1} > 2·ω^{f_0(ρι)+f_1(ρι)}，而这需要分 Φ_k 与 Ψ_k 四种组合逐一核对 f_0、f_1 在两个后继上的取值行为（1281-1287 行）。难点在于把「树在长」翻译成序数严格下降，且四种公式组合的不等式都必须成立；原文位置在证明的 1272-1277 行与 1281-1287 行。
